subject_session: sub-Achilles/ses-Achilles-10252013 (primary), plus Buddy-06272013, Cicero-09012014, Gatsby-08022013, Cicero-09172014

headline_stat.name: Fraction of active CA1 pyramidal cells with a significant place field in >=1 direction

stated_limitation: The linearized position is also left as NaN whenever the animal is off the track proper, in the reward areas past either end, so roughly 13 to 32% of MAZE samples carry a usable position depending on the session. That is the curation the original authors applied and it is exactly the restriction a one-dimensional place-field analysis wants.

justification.dataset: DANDI:000044 (Grosmark & Buzsaki hc-11 dorsal CA1 linear track) is the canonical choice for place fields, and the run used five sessions from four rats rather than one.
justification.handling: Real data streamed via LINDI with the position timebase explicitly reconstructed and asserted against the MAZE epoch duration, excitatory/inhibitory labels used for unit selection, and speed-thresholded direction-split run epochs.
justification.analysis: Occupancy-normalized rate maps, Skaggs information, and a proper circular-shift null inside the run epochs are all correct, but the place-cell criterion ORs two uncorrected alpha=0.05 directional tests per unit with no multiple-comparison correction, which inflates the effective alpha without changing the direction of the result.
justification.correctness: All reported numbers reproduce exactly from the notebook's stdout and are internally consistent, but the headline 82% falls above the preregistered 0.30-0.75 range, which caps this axis at 1.
justification.figures: Seven figures show the effect unambiguously with labeled units and sample sizes: example cells span the track and were gated on significance and SI > 0.5 before being ranked by peak rate for legibility, population maps show the diagonal collapsing across directions, and the null distributions and decoding controls are plotted.
justification.honesty: No claim is contradicted by the figures and the per-session variability is fully published, but the write-up does not flag that the 82% rests on an uncorrected two-direction OR test, is high relative to the literature, or that one of the five sessions sits close to its own null.
